# National Geographic

> > National Geographic's exploration and science journalism covering wildlife photography, space discoveries, archaeological findings, and natural world phenomena.

National Geographic delivers award-winning content spanning adventure, science, and exploration. The site features work from renowned photographers like Steve Winter, Frans Lanting, and Pete Muller, alongside groundbreaking reporting on astronomy, archaeology, and environmental science from locations including the Pantanal, Botswana, Peru, and beyond.

## Key Topics

- Wildlife Photography
- Space Exploration & Astronomy
- Archaeological Discoveries
- Exoplanets & Planetary Science
- Nature Photography
- NASA Missions
- Climate & Environmental Science
- Ancient Civilizations
- Marine Exploration
- Hubble Telescope
- Solar System Research
- Historical Expeditions
- Photo Journalism
- Scientific Discovery

## Space & Astronomy

- [Our Solar System May Have Millions of Twins](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/100108-solar-systems-like-ours-twins): Survey finds Jupiter-Saturn analogs suggest millions of habitable planets
- [Hubble Telescope at 20: NASA Astronomers' Top Photos](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/100424-hubble-telescope-20th-anniversary-pictures): NASA astronomers select top Hubble Telescope images for 20th anniversary
- [New Planet System May Be Most Populated Yet Found](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/101130-new-planets-found-solar-system-twin-science-space): HD 10180 planetary system may be closest solar system analog yet found
- [Three New "Plutos"? Possible Dwarf Planets Found](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/110811-three-new-dwarf-planets-pluto-kuiper-belt-space-science): Three potential dwarf planets discovered in Kuiper belt beyond Neptune
- ["Suicide" Comet Storm Hits Sun—Bigger Sun-Kisser Coming?](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/110117-comets-storm-sun-soho-nasa-sungrazing-science-space): Sungrazing comet swarm detected by SOHO may herald larger visitor

## Archaeological Discoveries

- [100th Anniversary of Roald Amundsen Reaching South Pole—How the Grueling Race Was Won](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/100th-anniversary-of-norwegian-roald-amundsen-reaching-south-polefind-out-how-the-grueling-race-was): Amundsen vs Scott: 100th anniversary of 1911 South Pole race
- [Jacques Cousteau Centennial: What He Did, Why He Matters](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/100611-jacques-cousteau-100th-anniversary-birthday-legacy-google): Jacques Cousteau's centennial highlights ocean exploration legacy
- [Pictures: Odd Maya Tomb Yields Jeweled Teeth, More](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/100721-maya-tomb-human-fingers-king-guatemala-science-pictures): Maya royal tomb at El Zotz, Guatemala reveals jeweled teeth and fingers
- [Pocahontas's Wedding Chapel Found at Jamestown](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/101110-pocahontas-wedding-chapel-jamestown-science): Archaeologists discover church where Pocahontas married John Rolfe
- [Pictures: Pagan-Cult Worship Objects Found](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/100616-israel-pagan-cult-tomb-objects-pictures): Bronze Age pagan ritual objects discovered at Tel Qashish, Israel
- [Ancient Popcorn Found—Made 2,000 Years Earlier Than Thought in Peru](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/120119-national-popcorn-day-corn-peru-archaeology-food-science): Peruvian popcorn discovery pushes corn domestication back 2,000 years

## Natural World & Exploration

- [Video: Giant Undersea Volcano Revealed](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/100714-indonesia-okeanos-volcano-exploration-vin-video): First footage of Kawio Barat underwater volcano near Indonesia
- [Vancouver 2010 to Be Warmest Winter Olympics Yet](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/100212-vancouver-2010-warmest-winter-olympics): Vancouver 2010 Winter Olympics faces warmest conditions in history
- [Did Olympic Athletes Peak in the 1980s?](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/100226-vancouver-2010-olympics-new-world-record): Study suggests athletic performance nearing human limits since 1980s
